document.abstract: Interactive television (ITV) has been around for many years, but has been handicapped by the limited capacity of analog delivery. With the transition to digital television broadcasting infrastructures around the world providing increased flexibility and greater downstream data rates to support interactive television content/services, the prospects for growth are high. This paper provides a tutorial on the standards issues involved, including aspects of interactive content carriage in the DTV broadcast, a comparison of declarative versus procedural content, and a review of approaches being considered by the relevant standards bodies.

authors.bio: Patrick Griffis is the director, worldwide TV standards and strategy, for the Microsoft TV Platform Group at Microsoft Corp. In this capacity, he is responsible for the development and implementation of Microsoft TV's standards strategy across a wide variety of markets and industries. He began his career at RCA, where he earned eight patents in television design. Griffis is a member of the board of the ATSC Forum and a past member of the ATSC executive committee. He is Microsoft's representative to the ITU-R sector and head of the U.S. delegation to ITU-R Study Group 6M on Multimedia. Griffis has written many papers on the future of TV and spoken on numerous panels for Microsoft, including the Nielsen's National Client Meeting, the World TV Forum, Broadcast Asia, the IBC Broadcast Conference, and the NAB show.
